page: Amazon Web Services c6g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit Arm-based AWS Graviton processors with the Neoverse-N1 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated physical CPU cores without hyperthreading, operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem incorporates 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. It includes hardware AES encryption acceleration but lacks x86-specific vector extension suites like AVX or AMX. The instance contains 16.0 GB of RAM, offering 2.0 GB per core to maintain a compute-oriented 1:2 resource ratio. Local ephemeral NVMe storage is absent, necessitating network-attached Amazon EBS storage, while network connectivity yields a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

In synthetic and application benchmarks, the c6g.2xlarge delivers solid multi-threaded performance alongside moderate memory bandwidth. In stress-ng and multi-core Geekbench evaluations, the server achieves average results for its class, recording 9.46 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and 9.39 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. However, single-threaded processing and instruction-heavy benchmarks reveal lower relative performance, as indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 960 and reduced throughput in single-threaded gzip and bzip3 compression. PassMark encryption testing is also reduced due to the architectural absence of x86-specific vector cryptographic instructions. Qualitatively, the Graviton hardware profile provides strong energy and resource density, delivering predictable dedicated core compute at a favorable cost-efficiency point compared to legacy architecture equivalents.

The c6g.2xlarge is best suited for scale-out containerized microservices, web server fleets, distributed caching nodes such as Redis, software compilation pipelines, and general multi-threaded compute workloads that do not rely on x86 vector extensions.
description: The Amazon Web Services c6g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 16.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), it offers a compute-focused resource profile. The processor features 32 MB of shared L3 cache and hardware AES encryption support, though x86 vector instructions like AVX are absent. Network connectivity provides a 2 Gbps baseline, and the instance relies on remote EBS storage with zero bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, c6g.2xlarge delivers middle-tier multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth performance, including 9.46 GB/sec web serving throughput and 9.39 million Redis SET operations per second, but exhibits lower single-threaded compression scores. This instance provides a cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded scale-out applications, container microservices, software builds, and cache layers.
